assigned_items.argument_summary:
Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let $U:H\to H$ be unitary, and let $\Pi_R,\Pi_L:H\to H$ be orthogonal projections. Write $H_R=\operatorname{ran}(\Pi_R)$ and $H_L=\operatorname{ran}(\Pi_L)$. The **projected-unitary encoding** (PUE) of this data is the linear map

$$A:H_R\to H_L,\qquad Ax=\Pi_L Ux.$$

Equivalently, its ambient-space compression is $\Pi_LU\Pi_R$, restricted to $H_R$ and regarded as taking values in $H_L$. The map $A$ is a contraction: $\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le1$.

Put $n=\dim H_R$, $m=\dim H_L$, and $r=\operatorname{rank}(A)$. A singular-value decomposition consists of orthonormal bases $v_1,\ldots,v_n$ of $H_R$ and $u_1,\ldots,u_m$ of $H_L$, and positive singular values $1\ge\sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_r>0$, such that

$$A=\sum_{j=1}^{r}\sigma_j|u_j\rangle\langle v_j|.$$

The remaining right basis vectors span $\ker A$ and the remaining left basis vectors span $\ker A^*$. Empty bases and sums are allowed when a dimension or the rank is zero. The pairing in each rank-one map is the root-linear-first Dirac conversion of [[def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion]].

An exact square block encoding is a special case: identify the system with the all-zero ancilla subspace and take $\Pi_L=\Pi_R$ equal to that subspace. Under the injection $J_a$ of [[def-qa-22-block-encoding]], the compression is $J_a^*UJ_a$; an exact $(\alpha,a,0)$ block encoding has compressed block $A/\alpha$.

Let $A:H_R\to H_L$ be the PUE map of [[def-qa-24-pue-svd-data]], with positive singular pairs $(\sigma_j,v_j,u_j)$. For every $0<\sigma_j<1$, set

$$w_j=\frac{(I-\Pi_R)U^*u_j}{\sqrt{1-\sigma_j^2}},\qquad \widetilde w_j=\frac{(I-\Pi_L)Uv_j}{\sqrt{1-\sigma_j^2}}.$$

The vectors $w_j$ form an orthonormal family in $\ker\Pi_R$ and the vectors $\widetilde w_j$ form an orthonormal family in $\ker\Pi_L$. In the input basis $(v_j,w_j)$ and output basis $(u_j,\widetilde w_j)$,

$$U\big|_{\operatorname{span}(v_j,w_j)}=\begin{pmatrix}\sigma_j&\sqrt{1-\sigma_j^2}\\\sqrt{1-\sigma_j^2}&-\sigma_j\end{pmatrix}.$$

For $\sigma_j=1$, $Uv_j=u_j$ and the complementary vector is absent. A right zero-singular vector $v\in\ker A\cap H_R$ satisfies $Uv\in\ker\Pi_L$; a left zero-singular vector $u\in\ker A^*\cap H_L$ satisfies $U^*u\in\ker\Pi_R$. Let $M_R$ be the orthogonal sum of all positive-singular input planes or lines, $\ker A$, and $U^*(\ker A^*)$; let $M_L$ be the corresponding sum of positive-singular output planes or lines, $U(\ker A)$, and $\ker A^*$. Then $U(M_R)=M_L$. The residual ambient subspaces $M_R^\perp$ and $M_L^\perp$ lie in $\ker\Pi_R$ and $\ker\Pi_L$, and $U(M_R^\perp)=M_L^\perp$. Thus each named block is invariant under its corresponding projector, with no implicit pairing of the two kernels.

Let $A:H_R\to H_L$ be the PUE map of [[def-qa-24-pue-svd-data]], with positive singular-value decomposition $A=\sum_{j=1}^{r}\sigma_j|u_j\rangle\langle v_j|$. Let $p:[-1,1]\to\mathbb C$ be a scalar function.

If $p$ is **odd**, define the odd singular-value transform by

$$p^{\mathrm{SV}}_{\mathrm{odd}}(A):H_R\to H_L,\qquad p^{\mathrm{SV}}_{\mathrm{odd}}(A)=\sum_{j=1}^{r}p(\sigma_j)|u_j\rangle\langle v_j|.$$

If $p$ is **even**, define its right-space transform by

$$p^{\mathrm{SV}}_{R}(A):H_R\to H_R,\qquad p^{\mathrm{SV}}_{R}(A)=\sum_{j=1}^{r}p(\sigma_j)|v_j\rangle\langle v_j|+p(0)\Pi_{\ker A},$$

where $\Pi_{\ker A}$ is the orthogonal projection in $H_R$ onto $\ker A$. The left-space version is

$$p^{\mathrm{SV}}_{L}(A):H_L\to H_L,\qquad p^{\mathrm{SV}}_{L}(A)=\sum_{j=1}^{r}p(\sigma_j)|u_j\rangle\langle u_j|+p(0)\Pi_{\ker A^*}.$$

The odd transform annihilates the right kernel because oddness gives $p(0)=0$; the even transforms use the canonical kernel projections. The resulting operators are independent of the chosen SVD by [[lem-qa-24-singular-transform-basis-independence]].

**Inputs.** A finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space $H$, a unitary $U:H\to H$, orthogonal projections $\Pi_R,\Pi_L$, an integer $d\ge0$, and an exact real phase list $\Phi=(\phi_0,\ldots,\phi_d)$. The input access contract states separately whether $U$, $U^*$, controlled-$U$, and controlled-$U^*$ are supplied and gives their individual costs. The scalar signal sequence is $U_\Phi(x)=Z(\phi_0)\prod_{j=1}^{d}(W_R(x)Z(\phi_j))$ from [[def-qa-23-qsp-signal-sequence]], with its admissible polynomial pair from [[def-qa-23-qsp-admissible-polynomial-pair]]. A desired polynomial target is supplied with a certificate that $\Phi$ realizes its scalar polynomial; generation of $\Phi$ is a separate classical/circuit input.

**Output.** The procedure returns the finite unitary sequence below and uses its compression from $H_R=\operatorname{ran}(\Pi_R)$ to $H_L=\operatorname{ran}(\Pi_L)$ for odd $d$, or from $H_R$ to itself for even $d$. No measurement or state-preparation circuit is implicit in this block description.

**Instructions.** For $d\ge0$, set the current side to $R$ and apply the projector phase $e^{i\phi_d(2\Pi_R-I)}$. For $j=d-1,d-2,\ldots,0$, apply $U$ and switch the current side from $R$ to $L$ if it is $R$; otherwise apply $U^*$ and switch from $L$ to $R$. Then apply $e^{i\phi_j(2\Pi_{\mathrm{current}}-I)}$. Thus there are $d$ alternating signal calls and $d+1$ projector-phase operations; $d=0$ has no signal call and consists only of the phase at $\Pi_R$.

For a real target polynomial, run the two phase lists $\Phi$ and $-\Phi$ in coherent control branches, with the control initialized in $|+\rangle$, and take the $|+\rangle$-to-$|+\rangle$ block. The procedure uses the reflected signal convention $W_R$ throughout. If a circuit is built through the alternative SU(2) convention, its control-dependent scalar phase must be retained as a relative phase. The exact block action, the real-part extraction, and the implementation costs are established in the separate theorem items on this page. Every phase list, inverse call, controlled call, phase rotation, and finite-gate compilation is supplied or charged separately.

For a finite-dimensional PUE map $A:H_R\to H_L$, the odd singular-value transform and both even singular-value transforms of [[def-qa-24-singular-value-transform]] are independent of the chosen singular-vector bases. On a positive singular-value subspace, $A/\sigma$ canonically pairs the right and left eigenspaces; on repeated singular values the transform is scalar on the whole corresponding subspace. The even transforms use the canonical orthogonal projection onto $\ker A$ or $\ker A^*$ with coefficient $p(0)$; the odd transform has no zero-singular cross term.

Let $\Pi$ be an orthogonal projection on a finite-dimensional space $H$, with reflection $R_\Pi=2\Pi-I$ and $S_\Pi=I-2\Pi=-R_\Pi$. Suppose the control-first call $C(R_\Pi)$ is explicitly supplied, together with an ancilla initialized in $|0\rangle$ and exact one-qubit $H$ and $R_z$ gates. Then the unitary $e^{i\phi R_\Pi}$ is implemented exactly by two controlled-reflection calls and one variable phase rotation, with a constant number of additional one-qubit gates, and the ancilla is returned to $|0\rangle$. If an external branch qubit is present and a branch-controlled $R_z(2\phi)$ is supplied, controlling only that rotation implements the controlled projector phase; the two controlled-reflection calls remain unconditional with respect to the external branch. In QSVT the construction is applied separately to $\Pi_R$ and $\Pi_L$; each projector-phase slot uses two controlled calls to the corresponding reflection. The access and gate costs are charged separately.

For degree $d\ge0$, one un-controlled QSVT sequence makes exactly $d$ signal calls: $\lceil d/2\rceil$ calls to $U$ and $\lfloor d/2\rfloor$ calls to $U^*$, beginning with $U$ when $d>0$. It applies exactly $d+1$ projector-phase operations, with $\lceil(d+1)/2\rceil$ about $\Pi_R$ and $\lfloor(d+1)/2\rfloor$ about $\Pi_L$. By [[thm-qa-24-projector-phase-implementation]], each phase operation uses two controlled calls to the corresponding reflection and one variable one-qubit phase rotation, plus a constant number of one-qubit gates. A coherent control of one sequence against the identity requires no controlled signal call when $d$ is even and one controlled signal call when $d$ is odd. Selecting between the two phase lists $\Phi$ and $-\Phi$ uses the same unconditioned signal list in both branches and controls only the phase rotations. Phase generation, inverse access, and finite-gate compilation retain their separately declared costs. At $d=0$ there is no signal or controlled-signal call.

Let $A:H_R\to H_L$ be the PUE map of [[def-qa-24-pue-svd-data]], with positive singular pairs $(\sigma_j,v_j,u_j)$, and let $\Phi=(\phi_0,\ldots,\phi_d)$ be the exact phase list in [[alg-qa-24-qsvt]]. Let $P_\Phi$ be the upper-left scalar polynomial of its QSP signal sequence. On every positive two-dimensional singular plane from [[lem-qa-24-pue-svd-invariant-subspaces]], the QSVT sequence is exactly $U_\Phi(\sigma_j)$. Consequently, if $d$ is odd,

$$\Pi_LU_\Phi\Pi_R\big|_{H_R}=\sum_{j=1}^{r}P_\Phi(\sigma_j)|u_j\rangle\langle v_j|=\bigl(P_\Phi\bigr)^{\mathrm{SV}}_{\mathrm{odd}}(A),$$

and if $d$ is even,

$$\Pi_RU_\Phi\Pi_R\big|_{H_R}=\sum_{j=1}^{r}P_\Phi(\sigma_j)|v_j\rangle\langle v_j|+P_\Phi(0)\Pi_{\ker A}=\bigl(P_\Phi\bigr)^{\mathrm{SV}}_R(A).$$

The formulas include singular values $0$ and $1$, repeated singular values, unmatched left and right kernels, and zero-dimensional singular spaces. If $p\in\mathbb R[x]$ has parity $d\bmod2$ and $|p(x)|\le1$ on $[-1,1]$, the exact completion and phase-factorization suppliers give a phase list with $\operatorname{Re}P_\Phi=p$. The coherent $\Phi$/$-\Phi$ branch then has compressed block $p^{\mathrm{SV}}(A)$; for a supplied uniform scalar error $\eta$, its block differs from $p^{\mathrm{SV}}(A)$ by at most $\eta$.

Let $A,B:H_R\to H_L$ be contractions between the same finite-dimensional complex-inner-product spaces, let $P$ be the scalar polynomial of an exact degree-$d$ QSVT phase sequence, and put $\delta=\|A-B\|_{\mathrm{op}}$. Then, for the corresponding odd or even singular-value transforms,

$$\|P^{\mathrm{SV}}(A)-P^{\mathrm{SV}}(B)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le4d\sqrt{\delta}.$$

For $d=0$ the transform is constant on the relevant singular space and the difference is zero. The lemma is an operator statement; the unitary completions used in the proof are finite-dimensional existence constructions and do not supply an efficient implementation or any additional query access.

Let $A:H_R\to H_L$ be a finite PUE map and let $p\in\mathbb R[x]$ have degree at most $d$, parity $d\bmod 2$, and $|p(x)|\le1$ on $[-1,1]$. The exact real-polynomial completion and phase-factorization results give a phase list $\Phi$ whose scalar QSP polynomial satisfies $\operatorname{Re}P_\Phi=p$. Run the degree-$d$ QSVT sequence with a control qubit prepared in $|+\rangle$, using the phase lists $\Phi$ and $-\Phi$ in its two branches, and project the control back onto $|+\rangle$. The resulting compressed block is exactly $p^{\mathrm{SV}}_{\mathrm{odd}}(A)$ for odd $d$, and exactly $p^{\mathrm{SV}}_R(A)$ for even $d$, including the even value $p(0)$ on $\ker A$. The result includes $d=0$, zero and unit singular values, repeated values, and unmatched kernels.

The two branches share the same $d$ unconditioned alternating calls to $U$ and $U^*$. Each of the $d+1$ projector-phase slots uses two controlled-reflection calls for its phase gadget and one branch-controlled one-qubit rotation; the controlled-rotation and reflection-access costs are charged separately. No controlled signal call is needed for the $\Phi/-\Phi$ selector. Phase-list generation and any finite-gate compilation remain separately charged.

Let $A$ be a finite square or rectangular matrix with a declared isometric padding $\widehat A$, and let $\alpha>0$ satisfy $\alpha\ge\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}$. Let $B$ be the exact compressed PUE block of the supplied input unitary and assume

$$\|B-\widehat A/\alpha\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{BE}}.$$

Let $P$ be the degree-$d$ parity polynomial of an admissible QSVT phase sequence, and let $f$ have the same parity. Put $S:=\{0\}\cup\{\sigma_j:\sigma_j>0\text{ is a singular value of }\widehat A/\alpha\}$, so zero is included even when the two matrix dimensions differ. If $\sup_{\sigma\in S}|P(\sigma)-f(\sigma)|\le\eta_{\mathrm{poly}}$, and the implemented phase operation at slot $\ell$ is a unitary within operator-norm error $\zeta_\ell$ of its ideal operation, then the implemented compressed block $\widetilde B$ satisfies

$$\|\widetilde B-f^{\mathrm{SV}}(\widehat A/\alpha)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\eta_{\mathrm{poly}}+4d\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{BE}}}+\sum_{\ell}\zeta_\ell.$$

The exact sequence uses $d$ calls alternating between $U$ and $U^*$, $d+1$ projector-phase operations, and the reflection and one-qubit resources in [[thm-qa-24-qsvt-query-count]]. A real-polynomial control wrapper has its separately listed controlled gates. Matrix-data access, block-encoding construction, inverse and controlled access, phase-list generation, finite-gate compilation, and classical bit costs are charged through their declared interfaces; no cost follows from a bare matrix.

A false extension of the odd singular-value formula that assigns a nonzero coefficient to zero-singular-vector pairs depends on arbitrary basis choices. Take $A=0:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$ and the scalar function $f(x)=1$. Pair the right zero vector $v=1$ with either left zero vector $u=1$ or $u=-1$. The resulting rank-one sums are respectively $I$ and $-I$, despite the same zero map $A$.

Let $0\le\sigma\le1$, $H=\mathbb C^2$, $U_\sigma=\begin{pmatrix}\sigma&\sqrt{1-\sigma^2}\\\sqrt{1-\sigma^2}&-\sigma\end{pmatrix}$, and $\Pi_R=\Pi_L=|0\rangle\langle0|$. The PUE block is the scalar matrix $A=[\sigma]$. Use the degree-one phase list $(0,0)$, whose scalar polynomial is $P(x)=x$.

transitive_suppliers.observed_excerpt:
All complex inner products in this track use the root convention: they are
linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second
([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). For vectors $x,y$ in the same
space, define the Dirac pairing by

$$\langle x|y\rangle_D:=\langle y,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}.$$

The ket $|x\rangle$ denotes the vector $x$. The bra $\langle x|$ denotes the
linear functional $z\mapsto\langle z,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}$.

For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H,K$, vectors $y\in H$ and
$x\in K$, define the rank-one linear map

$$|x\rangle\langle y|:H\to K,\qquad z\mapsto\langle z,y\rangle_{H,\mathrm{root}}x.$$

Given ordered orthonormal bases of $H$ and $K$, its coordinate matrix is
$[x][y]^\dagger$, where $[x]$ and $[y]$ are the corresponding coordinate
columns and $M^\dagger:=\overline M^{\mathsf T}$ is the conjugate transpose.
The coordinate assertion is established in
[[thm-qc-dirac-notation-coordinate-identity]].

transitive_suppliers.observed_excerpt:
Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces with ordered
orthonormal bases $E=(e_j)_{j<n}$ and $F=(f_i)_{i<m}$. Let $T:H\to K$ be
linear ([[def-linear-map]]), and write $T_{ij}$ for the $(i,j)$ entry of its
matrix in these bases.
Then, for every $z\in H$,

$$Tz=\sum_{j<n}\sum_{i<m}T_{ij}\langle z,e_j\rangle_{H,\mathrm{root}}f_i, \qquad T=\sum_{j<n}\sum_{i<m}T_{ij}|f_i\rangle\langle e_j|.$$

For $x\in K$ and $y\in H$, the rank-one map $|x\rangle\langle y|$ has
coordinate matrix $[x]_F[y]_E^\dagger$, where $M^\dagger=\overline M^{\mathsf T}$.
Its amplitude satisfies
$\langle x|T|y\rangle_D=\langle Ty,x\rangle_{K,\mathrm{root}}$.
All sums are empty when an index dimension is zero, and the identities include
those cases.

transitive_suppliers.observed_excerpt:
For $n\ge0$ and a binary word $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})\in\{0,1\}^n$, define its
**big-endian index**

$$\operatorname{enc}_n(x):=\sum_{k<n}x_k\,2^{\,n-1-k}.$$

Thus the first wire is the most significant bit. For $n=0$, the domain
$\{0,1\}^0$ consists only of the empty word $()$, and the empty sum gives
$\operatorname{enc}_0(())=0$. In an ordered $n$-qubit
computational basis, the word $x$ occupies the slot numbered
$\operatorname{enc}_n(x)$.

transitive_suppliers.observed_excerpt:
For an integer $d\ge 1$, the $d$-level register is the complex inner-product
space $Q_d=\mathbb C^d$ with the standard pairing
$\langle z,w\rangle_{\rm root}=\sum_{j<d}z_j\overline{w_j}$, linear in the
first argument as in [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]] and
[[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]. Its **computational basis** is the
ordered standard basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of [[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]].
The register's alphabet is the ordered set $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$.

For $n\ge0$, the $n$-qubit register is the ordered tensor product over
$\mathbb C$ of $n$ copies of $Q_2$. Here $\otimes_{\mathbb C}$ is the algebraic
module tensor product ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]),
with its complex-module structure and finite iterated/empty-product conventions
from [[thm-commutative-ring-module-structure-on-a-tensor-product]] and
[[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]. The tuple of
bit positions is ordered lexicographically, with the first wire as the most
significant position; the product-basis theorem below establishes the
corresponding elementary tensors as a basis. For $n=0$, the empty tensor
product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. This one-dimensional trivial
register is distinct from the zero vector space $\mathbb C^0$. By definition a
register has positive dimension; a zero-dimensional space may still occur as a
factor in the more general tensor-space construction below.

transitive_suppliers.observed_excerpt:
For a finite ordered family of finite-dimensional complex vector spaces
$H_k,K_k$ and complex-linear maps $T_k:H_k\to K_k$, the **tensor map**
$\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k:H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}\to
K_0\otimes\cdots\otimes K_{n-1}$ is the unique linear map satisfying

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)(x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes x_{n-1})=T_0x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes T_{n-1}x_{n-1}.$$

For $n=0$, the tensor map is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on the empty tensor
product $\mathbb C$.

transitive_suppliers.observed_excerpt:
An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

transitive_suppliers.observed_excerpt:
Let $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$ be a finite ordered list of finite-dimensional
complex inner-product spaces with specified ordered orthonormal bases of
sizes $d_0,\ldots,d_{n-1}$, allowing $d_k=0$. The elementary tensors of the
factor bases, ordered lexicographically, form an orthonormal basis of the
tensor register, and

$$\dim(H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1})=\prod_{k<n}d_k.$$

For the empty list the product is $1$ and the tensor space is $\mathbb C$; if
any $d_k=0$, the tensor space is zero and the product basis is empty.

Let $(T_k:H_k\to K_k)_{k<n}$ and $(S_k:K_k\to L_k)_{k<n}$ be finite ordered
families of linear maps between finite-dimensional complex inner-product
spaces. Then

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}S_k\right)\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)=\bigotimes_{k<n}(S_kT_k),\qquad \bigotimes_{k<n}I_{H_k}=I_{\otimes_{k<n}H_k},\qquad \left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)^*=\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k^*.$$

In the first formula, $S_kT_k$ means $S_k\circ T_k$. Here $I_{H_k}$ denotes
the identity map $x\mapsto x$. All adjoints use the
repository pairing, linear in the first argument. The empty tensor-map
identity is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on $\mathbb C$.

transitive_suppliers.observed_excerpt:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root library's convention that the inner product is linear in its first argument. A **density operator** on $H$ is a non-negative endomorphism $\rho:H\to H$ with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho)=1$; non-negative and trace have the meanings of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]] and [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. The zero-dimensional space is excluded: its only endomorphism has trace $0$.

Here $\ker\rho=\{x\in H:\rho x=0\}$, using the kernel of a linear map from [[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]. The **support** of $\rho$ is the orthogonal complement of its kernel in the root convention:

$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho):=\{x\in H: \langle x,y\rangle=0\text{ for every }y\in\ker\rho\}.$$

For a subspace $S\subseteq H$, $\rho$ is **faithful on $S$** when $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)=S$ and the restriction $\rho|_S:S\to S$ is positive definite in the sense of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]. This restriction is an endomorphism: if $x\in S$ and $y\in\ker\rho$, self-adjointness gives $\langle\rho x,y\rangle=\langle x,\rho y\rangle=0$, so $\rho x\in(\ker\rho)^\perp=S$.

transitive_suppliers.observed_excerpt: Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. Two nonzero vectors $x,y\in H$ represent the same **ray** when $y=\alpha x$ for some nonzero $\alpha\in\mathbb C$. A **pure state** is such a ray. If $u$ is a unit representative, its associated operator is $P_u=|u\rangle\langle u|$, with the bra, ket and outer-product convention of [[def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion]]. The theorem [[thm-qc-ray-projector-well-defined-and-bijective]] proves that this operator is a rank-one orthogonal projection independent of the chosen unit representative, so it is the operator representative of the pure state.

Let $Q_2$ be the qubit space of [[def-qc-qubit-and-bloch-representation]], and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $Q_2$ in the sense of [[def-qc-density-operator]]. Define its candidate Bloch coordinates in $\mathbb C^3$ by
$$r_j(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho\sigma_j)\quad(j\in\{x,y,z\}),\qquad \mathbf r(\rho):=(r_x(\rho),r_y(\rho),r_z(\rho)).$$
For any $\mathbf r=(r_x,r_y,r_z)\in\mathbb R^3$, define the associated Hermitian-matrix candidate
$$\rho(\mathbf r):=\frac12\bigl(I+r_xX+r_yY+r_zZ\bigr).$$
Write $\mathbf r\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}:=r_xX+r_yY+r_zZ$ and
$$\|\mathbf r\|_2:=\sqrt{r_x^2+r_y^2+r_z^2}.$$
The next theorem proves that these trace coordinates are real and that every Hermitian trace-one $2\times2$ matrix is uniquely $\rho(\mathbf r)$; the positivity theorem determines which real-coordinate candidates are states.

Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space and let $\Pi$ be an orthogonal projection on $H$. Fix the two signs

$$R_\Pi:=2\Pi-I,\qquad S_\Pi:=I-2\Pi=-R_\Pi.$$

Thus $R_\Pi$ acts as $+I$ on $\operatorname{ran}\Pi$ and $-I$ on $\ker\Pi$; $S_\Pi$ reverses those signs. They are not interchangeable inside a controlled block. For a unit vector $\psi$, the rank-one reflection is $R_\psi=2|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|-I$ with the Dirac convention of [[def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion]].

An access model counts a direct reflection as one primitive call only when that call is explicitly declared. Controlled reflection access is a separate declaration. If $|0\rangle$ is a specified unit input in the same space $H$, the state is prepared as $\psi=U|0\rangle$ for a declared unitary $U$, and a reflection is implemented by conjugating $R_0=2|0\rangle\langle0|-I$, the construction is $UR_0U^\dagger$ and its cost must include the calls to $U$, $R_0$, and $U^\dagger$. A state vector or matrix description alone implies neither an efficient reflection nor inverse access.

Fix an ordered orthonormal pair $e_0,e_1$ in a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. If a vector has nonzero coordinates $\alpha,\beta$ on this pair, its **relative phase** on these coordinates is

$$\eta:=\frac{\beta/\alpha}{|\beta/\alpha|}\in\mathbb C,\qquad |\eta|=1.$$

The relative phase is undefined when either coordinate is zero. It is unchanged by multiplying the whole vector by any nonzero complex scalar. It can distinguish rays: for the unit vectors $\psi_\eta=(e_0+\eta e_1)/\sqrt2$, distinct values of $\eta$ give distinct rank-one projectors and distinct rays.

Fix a finite gate alphabet $G$ with maximum arity $k:=\max(\{r(g):g\in G\}\cup\{0\})$ and a circuit from [[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]]. The declared **size** is the number of gate occurrences, equivalently $\sum_{t=1}^d|L_t|$; the declared **depth** is the number $d$ of explicit layers, not a minimum over alternate layerings; the **width** is the number $n$ of all wires, including workspace wires. The operation model may also assign weighted gate costs, classical bit costs, and query costs; these are separate coordinates and are summed over the calls actually made.

A workspace wire is an ancilla. A **clean-ancilla promise** specifies computational-basis zero states for the ancillas and requires their exact return for every allowed data input: if $U$ is the implemented unitary, $V_D$ is the declared data unitary, and $|0_A\rangle$ is the specified joint zero vector, then $U(x\otimes|0_A\rangle)=V_Dx\otimes|0_A\rangle$ for every allowed data vector $x$. A **dirty-ancilla promise** permits an arbitrary ancilla state independent of the data input; it may be correlated with an untouched reference. Exact dirty-ancilla restoration means the implemented unitary on data and ancillas is $V_D\otimes I_A$ on the entire joint space, where $V_D$ is the declared unitary on data. The same operator equality then holds after tensoring with the identity on any finite untouched reference. Consequently, product input between the data and the combined ancilla/reference system remains product after the operation. No uncorrelated-output claim is made for an initially data-correlated ancilla.

A controlled or inverse operation is counted only when the operation model explicitly grants that access or supplies a construction; its charge is recorded separately from an ordinary call unless the model explicitly combines them. In particular, the matrix of $U$ alone supplies neither a controlled call nor an inverse query, in accordance with [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]] and [[def-qc-inverse-unitary-access]].

Let $D$ be a finite ordered quantum register and let $A$ be an ordered register of $k\ge0$ ancilla qubits, with Hilbert spaces $\mathcal H_D$ and $\mathcal H_A$. Write $|0_A\rangle=|0^k\rangle$, including $|0_A\rangle=1$ when $k=0$. Let $U$ be a unitary on $\mathcal H_D\otimes\mathcal H_A$ and let $V$ be a unitary on $\mathcal H_D$.

The register $A$ is a **clean ancilla register for $U$ and $V$** when
$$
U(|\psi\rangle_D\otimes|0_A\rangle)=V|\psi\rangle_D\otimes|0_A\rangle
$$
for every vector $|\psi\rangle_D$. Thus the data operation is independent of the input vector and all clean wires return exactly to zero.

The register $A$ is a **dirty ancilla register for $U$ and $V$** when the operator identity $U=V\otimes I_A$ holds on $\mathcal H_D\otimes\mathcal H_A$. Equivalently, every product input $|\psi\rangle_D\otimes|\eta\rangle_A$ is mapped to $V|\psi\rangle_D\otimes|\eta\rangle_A$, with the same $V$ for every data and ancilla vector. This requires exact restoration of an arbitrary, initially unknown ancilla state and forbids residual data–ancilla correlation.

These are exact contracts for the complete subroutine. A temporary intermediate alteration of an ancilla is permitted if the full unitary satisfies the stated identity.
